title: The fruits of Communion (CCC 1391–1401)
hookLine: union with Christ, forgiveness of venial sin, unity, care for the poor

lines: THE LIST ENDS ON THE STREET.
cards: Right after Communion, the Mass goes quiet. People file back from the front and kneel or sit. Some close their eyes.
A child swings her feet. The organist plays something soft, or nothing at all. It can look like nothing is happening.
The Catechism disagrees. It lists what Communion does in a person, and the list doesn't stop at the pew. It ends somewhere unexpected: out on the street, with people who are hungry.

teach.b: First, union with Christ. The Catechism quotes Jesus in John's Gospel, in the Douay-Rheims: "He that eateth my flesh, and drinketh my blood, abideth in me, and I in him." Abiding: staying, living with.
What bread does for the body, Communion does for the life of grace begun at baptism: it keeps it, grows it, renews it.
Second, separation from sin. The body given up for us and the blood shed for the forgiveness of sins can't unite people to Christ without also cleansing them.
Communion strengthens charity, the Catechism says, and charity wipes away venial sins, the everyday ones, and helps protect against grave sin in the future.
It's careful to add that Communion isn't meant for forgiving mortal sins; that belongs to the sacrament of penance. Third, unity.

Paul puts it in one line: "For we, being many, are one bread, one body, all that partake of one bread." So the Eucharist makes the Church. Receiving Christ's body joins people to everyone else who receives it.
And last, the one on the street.

teach.h: THE POOR: CHRIST'S BROTHERS AND SISTERS.
teach.b: To receive in truth the body and blood of Christ given up for us, the Catechism says, we must recognize Christ in the poorest, his brothers and sisters.

teach.h: WE, BEING MANY, ARE ONE BREAD.
teach.b: It cites John Chrysostom, who warned people who had tasted the Lord's blood against failing to recognize their own brother in need.
Then, honestly, the section ends with a sorrow: Christians who can't yet share one table, and a hope that they one day will.

how: After receiving Communion, Catholics spend a few moments in silent thanksgiving; some parishes take up a collection for the poor at Mass or keep food bins by the church doors.

games.q: what does “the fruits of communion” mean?
o: union, freedom from sin, one body, care for the poor
the bread and wine left over after Mass is finished
good feelings that come right after receiving

p: abideth in me, and I in him

s: the Catechism says Communion is mainly a private moment between a person and God
it says Communion joins people to one another, and commits them to the poor.
Communion is meant for forgiving mortal sins
the Catechism says that belongs to the sacrament of penance; Communion wipes away venial sins.
the Catechism compares Communion to ordinary food
what bread does for the body, Communion does for the life of grace.

games.q: you've just received Communion and walked out of church. someone at the door asks for help. what does the Catechism tie to receiving in truth?
o: getting home quickly to keep the moment private.
praying for them later, from a distance.
games.why: the Catechism says that to receive in truth the body and blood of Christ, we must recognize Christ in the poorest.

practice: Think of the walk out of church, or out of your front door: someone asking for change, a food bank bin, a neighbor who's struggling and doesn't say so.

Choose one concrete gift, money, food, an hour, a phone call, small enough that you'll really give it, and hold that person or place in mind while you breathe. If you pray, bring them to the altar with you.

wordCard.voice: The fruits of Communion. Union with Christ, separation from sin, unity in one body, and care for the poor, his brothers and sisters. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: sharing, fellowship; the word in Paul's letters behind 'communion' with the body and blood of Christ.

carryVoice: Your line: communion makes communion. The table and the street belong together. Until tomorrow.
